title_en: Sun Wei v. Nantong Baichuan Flour Co., Ltd. — dispute over unjust enrichment

full_text_en:
Sun Wei v. Nantong Baichuan Flour Co., Ltd. — dispute over unjust enrichment

Ruling Summary

The amount of illicit money determined in a criminal judgment is not equivalent to the scope of losses caused by the crime, and the scope of losses cannot be determined simply based on the amount of illicit money found in the criminal judgment. The standard of proof in criminal cases differs from that in civil cases, and the high standard of criminal cases should not replace the civil standard of proof.

Plaintiff: Sun Wei, female, 34 years old, residing in Hai'an County, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Nantong Baichuan Flour Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hebin West Road, Hai'an Town, Hai'an County.

Plaintiff Sun Wei initiated a lawsuit against Defendant Nantong Baichuan Flour Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baichuan Company) for a dispute over unjust enrichment, and filed the case with the Hai'an County People's Court of Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff Sun Wei alleged: She originally served as a warehouse keeper for Baichuan Company. In 2011, after Baichuan Company discovered the duty-related encroachment by her, Yang Jianjun, and Zhang Ronggen, they negotiated and agreed to settle internally for RMB 400,000, without pursuing criminal liability. After the oral agreement was reached, Sun Wei entrusted another person to deposit RMB 400,463.92 into Baichuan Company's account, but was nonetheless reported and criminally prosecuted. In 2013, the criminal judgment of the court determined that Sun Wei had unlawfully taken a total of RMB 100,000 of the company's property. Therefore, the excess refund of RMB 300,463.92 should constitute unjust enrichment for Baichuan Company. She requested the court to order Defendant Baichuan Company to return the unjust enrichment of RMB 300,463.92 plus interest of RMB 54,000, and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant Baichuan Company argued: The losses caused to the company's property by Plaintiff Sun Wei and others, after audit, amounted to RMB 721,881. After the company discovered the encroachment, Sun Wei and others negotiated with the company to avoid criminal prosecution, and orally agreed to refund RMB 400,463.92, which was not refunded solely by Sun Wei. During the criminal trial of the duty-related encroachment case involving Sun Wei and others at the Hai'an County People's Court, Sun Wei admitted that she had no objection to the audit report, and the audit report showed that the property taken by Sun Wei and others exceeded the amount refunded. The criminal judgment identified the illicit money as RMB 100,000, which did not represent the full extent of the property taken by Sun Wei and others, and Sun Wei's claim for a refund through civil proceedings lacked a basis. She requested the court to dismiss Sun Wei's claims.

The Hai'an County People's Court of Jiangsu Province found the following facts upon trial:

In 2004, Plaintiff Sun Wei began serving as a warehouse keeper for Baichuan Company. In 2011, Defendant Baichuan Company suspected that Sun Wei, together with accountant Yang Jianjun and production shift supervisor Zhang Ronggen, had jointly taken flour and bran belonging to the company. When the company approached Sun Wei for a discussion, she denied the accusations. Baichuan Company then commissioned Jiangsu Zhongzheng Tongren Accounting Firm Co., Ltd. to conduct a special audit of the custody of finished products in the company's inventory from May 2008 to December 2010, as well as related internal controls and financial management. On March 26, 2011, Zhongzheng Tongren issued the Special Audit Report on the Custody of Finished Products of Nantong Baichuan Flour Co., Ltd. (Tongren Special Audit No. 239 of 2011). Sun Wei paid the audit fee of RMB 20,000. After the audit results were released, Sun Wei, Yang Jianjun, and Zhang Ronggen admitted to the unlawful taking of company property and requested that the company not pursue criminal liability. They orally negotiated a refund agreement, under which Sun Wei and others would refund RMB 400,463.92 to Baichuan Company. Through her relative Shao Junlan, Sun Wei deposited RMB 400,463.92 into Baichuan Company's account in two installments on April 10, 2011, and April 26, 2011. This amount included RMB 100,000 refunded by Yang Jianjun and Zhang Ronggen.

On October 21, 2011, after receiving a tip-off from the public, the Nantong Public Security Bureau referred the case involving suspected duty-related encroachment by Sun Wei, Yang Jianjun, and Zhang Ronggen to the Hai'an County Public Security Bureau for criminal investigation. On December 16, 2013, the Hai'an County People's Court issued Criminal Judgment (2013) An Xing Er Chu Zi No. 0195, finding Sun Wei, Yang Jianjun, and Zhang Ronggen guilty of duty-related encroachment, and sentencing all three to suspended sentences. The three did not appeal. The criminal judgment found that: From January 2007 to October 2009, Sun Wei, while serving as warehouse keeper for Baichuan Company and taking advantage of her position in recording the quantities of flour and bran entering and leaving the warehouse, privately sold surplus flour and bran through others at market prices, obtaining RMB 20,000 which she kept for herself. From October 2009 to October 2010, Sun Wei, Yang Jianjun, and Zhang Ronggen, during the process of verifying the quantities of flour and bran entering the warehouse, underrecorded the quantities and had the surplus flour and bran sold by Sun Wei through others at market prices, obtaining RMB 80,000. Sun Wei, Yang Jianjun, and Zhang Ronggen divided the illicit money of RMB 80,000 in a 4:4:2 ratio. After the case was discovered, Sun Wei, Yang Jianjun, and Zhang Ronggen compensated the victim entity for all economic losses.

The facts found in the criminal judgment were essentially consistent with those in the Proposed Indictment (Haigong (Jing) Su Zi [2013] No. 393) of the Hai'an County Public Security Bureau, the Indictment (Haijian Su Xing Su [2013] No. 453) of the Hai'an County People's Procuratorate, and the Sentencing Recommendation (Haijian Su Xing Liang Jian [2013] No. 453) of the Hai'an County People's Procuratorate, which gradually narrowed the direct illicit money obtained by Sun Wei, Yang Jianjun, and Zhang Ronggen from over RMB 100,000 to RMB 100,000, and specified that the three had actively compensated the victim entity for all economic losses.

On December 3, 2011, when Sun Wei was interrogated by the Economic Investigation Brigade of Hai'an County Public Security Bureau, she stated: "In 2007, I started selling the flour I was keeping, mainly selling it to Li Fengying, who runs a flour and noodle business in a shop near the Baichuan Company gate. On October 10, 2010, the company asked me to submit the daily inventory numbers, but I couldn't. Around October 20, after I handed over the warehouse accounts to the company, I was suspended from the warehouse keeper position, my salary was stopped, and the company began auditing my accounts. The company's chairman Tang Changgen and party secretary Huang Zhaolong first talked to me, but I didn't admit to selling the warehouse goods at that time. After the audit report came out, the company approached me again, and I admitted to selling the warehouse goods. I also wrote a confession and submitted it to the company, admitting to selling over a hundred thousand yuan worth of goods. At that point, I couldn't face the company myself, so I asked my husband's sister Shao Junlan to handle it. Shao Junlan works at the City Agricultural Bank. Shao Junlan asked me how much I had taken, but I really couldn't recall the exact amount, only saying it was over a hundred thousand yuan. Shao Junlan made the decision for me: a little over 130,000 yuan. I discussed the refund with Yang Jianjun and Zhang Ronggen. Yang Jianjun returned RMB 20,000 to me, and Zhang Ronggen returned a total of RMB 80,000. Shao Junlan deposited the money into the company's account on my behalf, totaling RMB 135,463.92 including interest. After Shao Junlan made the refund, the company called me many times, saying that according to the audit report, nearly one million yuan worth of goods was missing, and they demanded I refund at least RMB 400,000. Later, Shao Junlan again handled it for me and negotiated with the company to refund RMB 400,000, requesting that the company not report the case."

Separately, it was found that the Special Audit Report on the Custody of Finished Products of Nantong Baichuan Flour Co., Ltd. (Tongren Special Audit No. 239 of 2011) stated that Zhongzheng Tongren had inspected the warehouse custody from May 2008 to December 2010 and found the following issues: (1) Based on the monthly receipts and disbursements reports and inventory lists provided by Sun Wei, it was found that: (a) The monthly report and inventory list for May 20, 2009 showed that the actual inventory of flour was 141,825 kg less than the book amount, and bran was 3,880 kg less than the book amount; (b) The monthly report and inventory list for November 20, 2010 showed that the actual inventory of flour was 126,775 kg less than the book amount, and bran was 60,120 kg less than the book amount. When the auditors questioned Sun Wei, the then warehouse keeper, about these issues, she gave no reasonable explanation. Regarding this audit report, during the criminal trial of the duty-related encroachment case involving Sun Wei and others on December 12, 2013, when cross-examining the testimony of Tang Changgen, Sun Wei stated: "The auditors were all friends Tang Changgen invited from Nanjing, and I don't agree that the audit results showing the company's losses were caused by my taking." However, during later cross-examination of the audit report itself, Sun Wei explicitly stated that she had no objection.

Audit participant Liu Ming testified in court that the above audit results had accounted for reasonable losses, and adding the figures directly could represent the losses of Baichuan Company between May 2008 and November 20, 2010. The litigation representatives of both parties jointly searched the Nantong Grain Network and learned that the minimum ex-factory price of Hai'an special first-grade flour between May 2008 and November 20, 2010 was RMB 2,680 per ton, consistent with certificates issued by Haifeng Rice Hai'an Co., Ltd. and Taixing Suzhong Flour Mill Co., Ltd. Sun Wei did not produce contrary evidence on the price issue, nor did she apply for an appraisal within the time limit set by the court. During the trial, Sun Wei admitted that the flour she had taken was special first-grade or above.

At the second trial, Sun Wei adjusted her claims to RMB 248,463.92 plus interest of RMB 54,000, calculated as total refund of RMB 400,463.92 minus the refund of RMB 100,000 by Yang Jianjun and Zhang Ronggen minus the illicit money amount of RMB 52,000 determined for Sun Wei in the criminal judgment, equaling RMB 248,463.92.

The Hai'an County People's Court of Jiangsu Province held at first instance:

A party has the burden to provide evidence to prove its claims, except as otherwise provided by law; otherwise, it shall bear adverse consequences. In this case, Plaintiff Sun Wei initiated a civil action based on unjust enrichment and should provide evidence to prove that the property losses caused to Baichuan Company by her individual and joint taking were lower than the orally agreed refund amount of RMB 400,463.92. Based on the existing evidence, the evidence provided by Sun Wei did not meet the standard of proof. The reasons are as follows:

First, the oral refund agreement of RMB 400,463.92 was the product of consensus between both parties and did not violate legal provisions. On December 3, 2011, when Sun Wei was interrogated by the Economic Investigation Brigade of Hai'an County Public Security Bureau, she stated, "Shao Junlan handled it for me and negotiated with the company to refund RMB 400,000," which is consistent with the allegations and defenses of both parties in this trial. Therefore, the oral refund agreement of RMB 400,463.92 was reached legally and voluntarily by both parties, without duress, fraud, or other illegal circumstances. As for the issue of whether to report the case, since the crime of duty-related encroachment is a public prosecution case, the victim has no right to decide whether and how the law should deal with it, and this cannot be a basis for determining the validity of the agreement.

Second, the audit report, having been accepted by both parties, should be used as evidence in this case to determine the scope of losses. In the above interrogation, Sun Wei stated that she confessed to the crime only after the audit report was issued, and during the criminal trial, she did not object to the audit report itself when directly cross-examining it, while in this trial she admitted to paying the audit fee of RMB 20,000. Therefore, although the audit report was commissioned unilaterally by Baichuan Company, where the law does not entirely prohibit the use of unilaterally commissioned appraisal reports as evidence, and Sun Wei, as the opposing party, ultimately accepted the report in the criminal trial, the report can be used as a basis for calculating losses. Sun Wei requested a re-appraisal of the audit report but did not provide sufficient evidence to rebut it, so the court denied her application.

Third, the amount of illicit money determined in a criminal judgment is not equivalent to the scope of losses caused by the crime, and the scope of losses cannot be determined simply by the amount of illicit money found in the criminal judgment. Typically, the scope of direct and indirect losses caused by a criminal act to the victim is larger than the illicit money directly obtained by the perpetrator. When handling civil compensation disputes arising from criminal acts, the basis for compensation is the victim's losses, not the illicit money directly obtained by the perpetrator. Sun Wei's claim in this litigation essentially conflates the amount of illicit money determined in the criminal judgment with the scope of the victim's losses, which is inconsistent with basic legal principles.

Fourth, the standard of proof in criminal cases differs from that in civil cases, and the high standard of criminal cases should not replace the civil standard of proof. Legal issues should be addressed with modern legal thinking and methods. With the rapid development of the times, the civil standard of proof has been separated from the criminal standard of proof, establishing its own independent system, and people should not completely import criminal proof thinking into civil proof. Criminal cases emphasize clear facts and conclusive evidence, while civil cases adopt the preponderance of the evidence rule, allowing "presumptions" based on certain evidence and comprehensive judgment according to everyday experience. Relatively speaking, the civil standard of proof is generally lower than the criminal standard of proof. In the criminal case, the amount of illicit money attributed to Sun Wei was gradually compressed and fixed from over RMB 100,000 to RMB 100,000, reflecting the strict evidence standard of criminal cases. In this case, the statements of both parties, Sun Wei's confession in the criminal case, the audit report, and witness testimony are essentially consistent, and under the preponderance of the evidence standard, the relevant facts are sufficiently proven. Even if the losses from bran are not included, calculated only at the minimum ex-factory price of flour at the time of the incident, the losses for which Sun Wei could not give a reasonable explanation during her tenure as warehouse keeper amount to over RMB 710,000 solely for flour [(141,825 kg + 126,775 kg) ÷ 1,000 × RMB 2,680/ton], far exceeding the orally agreed refund amount of RMB 400,463.92.

In summary, the evidence provided by Plaintiff Sun Wei in this case was insufficient to prove that the property losses caused to Defendant Baichuan Company by her individual and joint taking were lower than RMB 400,463.92, and her claim that Defendant Baichuan Company had unjust enrichment lacked legal and factual basis. The court did not accept it. Accordingly, the Hai'an County People's Court of Jiangsu Province, in accordance with Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 2 and Article 28 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, rendered the following judgment on July 15, 2014:

All claims of Plaintiff Sun Wei were dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant appealed, and the judgment has taken legal effect.
